description.narrative: OPC-programmet i Albanien är inriktat på två huvudområden: 1) medborgardeltagande och 2) arbetstagares rättigheter. OPC samarbetar med albanska fackföreningar, organisationer för arbetstagares rättigheter och POP-nätverket (ett nätverk av 13 lokalt baserade organisationer) för att uppnå programmets huvudmål, nämligen att Albanien ska stärka kapaciteten och legitimiteten hos det civila samhällets organisationer och stödja verksamhet som säkerställer att politiska, sociala och ekonomiska processer är delaktiga. Den typ av aktiviteter som genomförs i denna insats omfattar bland annat offentliga forum med valkandidater, övervakning och förespråkande av genomförandet av sociala kontrakt på lokal nivå, drift av ett resursnav och en arbetsakademi för att stödja nya fackföreningar och fackföreningsmedlemmar, observation av kränkningar av arbetstagares rättigheter, juridisk utbildning av arbetstagare, utbyte med liknande organisationer i regionen, Kapacitetsuppbyggande verksamhet och samarbete med internationella arbetarrörelseorganisationer.

The OPC programme in Albania focuses on two main areas: 1) citizen participation and 2) labour rights. OPC partners with Albanian trade unions, labour right organisations and POP network (a network of 13 locally based organisations) to achieve the main objective of the programme and that is Albania is to the capacity and legitimacy of civil society organisations and support activities that ensure the participatory nature of political, social and economic processes. The type of activities implemented in this intervention include among others public forums with elections’ candidates, monitoring and advocating for the implementation of Social Contracts at the local level, running of a resource hub and labour academy to support new trade unions and unionists, observing violations of labour rights, legal education of workers, exchange with similar organisations in the region, capacity building activities and collaboration with international labour movement organisations.

The objective of the programme is to strengthen the capacity and legitimacy of civil society organisations and support activities that ensure the participatory nature of political, social and economic processes. Civil society organisations will empower citizens to claim and exercise their rights and contribute to the advancement of good governance and socio-economic rights.

title.narrative: Decision on contribution OPC Programme Albania 2023-2027

description.narrative:
Thematic Area: Citizens Participation in Good Governance
Through a combination of public forums, systematic monitoring, and advocacy around Social Contracts, the POP Network project contributed to a more structured and meaningful civic engagement, particularly among women, youth, and marginalized groups.
- A key result was the increased involvement in decision-making processes with over 550 citizens directly engaged with 42 parliamentary candidates through seven public forums, reaching more than 23 000 viewers online. These platforms helped shift political discourse toward substantive issues such as governance, transparency, and social services, while strengthening citizens confidence to demand accountability.
- At the local level, continuous monitoring of around 130 municipal council meetings and the publication of monitoring reports for ten municipalities helped sustain institutional dialogue and improve responsiveness of duty bearers. This contributed to tangible progress in implementing Social Contract commitments, with concrete results in several municipalities. 51% of identified priorities of the Social Contracts 2023-2027 were integrated into municipal agendas or budgets.
- A good example is in Vau i Dejës municipality, where a community-led advocacy campaign collected 520 signatures for the establishment of the municipalitys first kindergarten with meals and longer opening hours to support working mothers. The initiative was successfully approved by the Municipal Council and will be included in the municipal budget.
Thematic Area: Socio-Economic/Labour Rights
Efforts in 2025 focused on empowering workers and strengthening social dialogue, contributing to increased awareness of labour rights and gradual improvements in collective organising. Worker engagement has grown, particularly in the oil, waste management, and health sectors with strong signals of rising momentum in labour mobilization. Institutionally, cooperation with the Labour Inspectorate has improved, although engagement with private companies remains uneven. Programme partners reinforced their engagement in policy monitoring, advocacy, and direct workers support, leading to impactful results (examples below):
- Wage increases for public cleaning workers in Elbasan: the dialogue led by LRER between workers, the Municipality of Elbasan, and sanitation companies resulted in a wage increase of 12.5 % for waste transport workers and promised increases of 37.5 % for day work and 50 % for night work for street cleaners, representing both improved incomes and an important step towards stronger social dialogue.
- SPSHSH increased its membership with 300 new members bringing the total number to 1410, with workers showing greater confidence in addressing violations and engaging with the union and reporting of employment rights violations becoming more frequent with improved use of legal channels and collective organizing.
- SKOTs legal advice services expanded to meet increasing demand on conflicts concerning labour contracts, dismissals and working hours. In 2025 SKOT secured four significant court victories that reinforced members rights. One of the cases involved an illegal dismissal from of an Albacall center employee that resulted in compensation payments, demonstrating the unions capacity to protect individual workers.
- GADC continued systematic reporting of labour right violations to the State Labour Inspectorate and Free Legal Aid Service (FLAS). These actions prompted official inspections, and enforcement measures, particularly improving protections for women and migrant workers in garment and footwear companies.
An external mid-term evaluation of the programme was conducted in the late 2025. The evaluation finds the programme to be highly relevant to Albanias socio-political context and the needs of rights holder. The Programme has been effective in strengthening partners institutional capacities, legitimacy, and collective influence. According to the evaluation report, the programme has achieved clear early outcomes toward its overall objective (impact) of more transparent, participatory, and accountable political and socio-economic processes.
